deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): for a prime a, Euler sorts the residues mod 4a that are ≡1 (mod 4) and prime to a into two classes. The class '4r+1' consists of the odd squares reduced mod 4a. The class '4ϱ+1' consists of the other admissible residues ≡1 (mod 4). His theorems: if the prime p=2m+1 satisfies p ≡ ±(4r+1) (mod 4a), then a^m ≡ 1 (mod p), so a is a quadratic residue. If p ≡ ±(4ϱ+1) (mod 4a), then a^m ≡ -1 (mod p). In modern terms: (a/p) depends only on p mod 4a, and (a/p)=1 iff p ≡ ±x^2 (mod 4a) with x odd. This is Euler's form of quadratic reciprocity.

This page:

(1) Periodicity. Each series repeats with period 4a. The first period is the admissible n ≡ 1 (mod 4) with n < 4a; later periods add 4a each time. So the test for p depends only on p mod 4a.

(2) Counting. Each period contains (a-1)/2 terms of each class. Reason (mine): of the a numbers ≡1 (mod 4) below 4a, exactly one is divisible by a. The squares form an index-2 subgroup of the remaining a-1 classes in (Z/4aZ)^*.

(3) Square property. Every 4r+1 is a square or becomes one on adding a multiple 4an. No 4ϱ+1 + 4an is ever a square. This is just the definition of the classes restated.

(4) Problem: treat composite a = fg with f, g distinct primes.
- Let P lie in both f(4r+1) and g(4r+1).
- If p = 4f p' ± P then f^m ≡ 1 (mod p). If p = 4g q ± P then g^m ≡ 1.
- Taking p' = gn and q = fn gives p = 4fgn ± P (a CRT combination mod 4fg). Then f^m ≡ g^m ≡ 1, so (fg)^m ≡ 1.
- Likewise, if P lies in both ϱ-classes, f^m ≡ g^m ≡ -1, so a^m = (fg)^m ≡ (+1).
- So the r-class for a is the union of (r∩r) and (ϱ∩ϱ). The ϱ-class for a is the mixed intersections (r∩ϱ) and (ϱ∩r).
- Implicit (mine): the mixed cases give a^m ≡ (+1)(-1) = -1, because f^m and g^m are each ≡ ±1 by Euler's criterion.
- Modern statement: (fg/p) = (f/p)(g/p).

(5) Corollary 1. If a = f^2, every 4n+1 (prime to f) is in the r-class and the ϱ-class is empty. Indeed a^m - 1 = f^{2m} - 1 = f^{p-1} - 1 is divisible by p (Fermat).

(6) Example I: a = 6, 4a = 24.
- 2-classes: 2r ≡ 1 (mod 8), 2ϱ ≡ 5 (mod 8).
- 3-classes: 3r ≡ 1 (mod 12), 3ϱ ≡ 5 (mod 12).
- r∩r: 1 (mod 24), giving 1, 25, 49, 73, 97.
- ϱ∩ϱ: 5 (mod 24).
- 2r∩3ϱ: 17. 3r∩2ϱ: 13.
- Table: r: 1, 5 | 25, 29, 49, 53, 73, 77, 97, 101. ϱ: 13, 17 | 37, 41, 61, 65, 85, 89.
- Result: (6/p)=1 iff p ≡ 1, 5, 19, 23 (mod 24).

(7) Example 2: a = 10, 4a = 40.
- 5-classes: 5r ≡ 1, 9 (mod 20); 5ϱ ≡ 13, 17 (mod 20).
- r∩r: 1, 9. ϱ∩ϱ: 13, 37. 2r∩5ϱ: 17, 33. 5r∩2ϱ: 21, 29.
- Table: r: 1, 9, 13, 37 | 41, 49, 53, 77, 81, 89, 93. ϱ: 17, 21, 29, 33 | 57, 61, 69, 73, 97.
- Result: (10/p)=1 iff p ≡ ±1, ±3, ±9, ±13 (mod 40).
errors: The claim that each period has (a-1)/2 terms in each class holds only for odd prime a. For a=2 each period (length 8) has one term per class. For composite a=fg the count is φ(4a)/4 per class, which Euler does not state.
Tacit restriction: residues divisible by a (e.g. 5 for a=5 or 10; 9, 21 for a=3 or 6) must be excluded, and 2m+1 must be a prime not dividing a. These are respected in the tables but not stated.
The composite-case argument only states the 'if' direction for the ϱ-class. That mixed cases give a^m ≡ -1 needs Euler's criterion (f^m ≡ ±1). This is correct but left implicit.

The whole procedure rests on the unproved prime case, i.e. quadratic reciprocity. Euler acknowledges on the previous page that 'demonstratio desideratur'. Not an error, but the results are conjectural in the text.
All numerical tables on this page check out against Legendre symbols; no arithmetic slips found.

results.what: Whether a^m ≡ ±1 mod the prime 2m+1 (i.e. (a/p)) depends only on p mod 4a, with residue classes ±(odd squares) mod 4a.
results.modern_name: Euler's form of the law of quadratic reciprocity
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (conjectured 1744–1783, E552 Opuscula analytica 1783); proved by Gauss 1796/1801; Legendre 1785/1798

results.what: Residue classes for composite a=fg obtained by intersecting the classes for f and g: r = (r∩r) ∪ (ϱ∩ϱ), ϱ = mixed intersections.
results.modern_name: Multiplicativity of the Legendre symbol in the numerator; Chinese remainder theorem combination of the characters p ↦ (f/p), (g/p) (Kronecker symbol as a character mod 4a)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler/Legendre (multiplicativity); Jacobi/Kronecker for the symbol formalism

results.what: For a a perfect square, every prime p ∤ a has a^m ≡ 1; the ϱ-class is empty.
results.modern_name: Fermat's little theorem / squares are residues

results.what: Explicit tables: (6/p)=1 iff p≡±1,±5 mod 24; (10/p)=1 iff p≡±1,±3,±9,±13 mod 40.

deep.surprise_reason: This is Euler's well-known empirical form of quadratic reciprocity, extended to composite a by multiplicativity, with correct tables. The same material appears in his published E552 (1783) and these Adversaria fragments were printed in the Opera Postuma (1862). Nothing here goes beyond what is already attributed to him.

checkable.sympy: all(legendre_symbol(6,p)==(1 if p%24 in (1,5,19,23) else -1) for p in primerange(5,5000))
checkable.asserts: Example I: 6 is a QR mod p iff p ≡ ±1, ±5 (mod 24)

checkable.sympy: all(legendre_symbol(10,p)==(1 if p%40 in (1,9,13,37,39,31,27,3) else -1) for p in primerange(7,5000))
checkable.asserts: Example 2: 10 is a QR mod p iff p ≡ ±1, ±3, ±9, ±13 (mod 40)

checkable.sympy: all(sorted({(x*x)%(4*a) for x in range(1,4*a,2) if gcd(x,a)==1})==sorted([n for n in range(1,4*a,4) if gcd(n,a)==1 and n in {(y*y)%(4*a) for y in range(1,4*a,2)}]) and len({(x*x)%(4*a) for x in range(1,4*a,2) if gcd(x,a)==1})==(a-1)//2 for a in primerange(3,60))
checkable.asserts: For odd prime a, the r-class (odd squares prime to a, mod 4a) has (a-1)/2 elements per period

checkable.sympy: all((pow(a,(p-1)//2,p)==1)==any((p-s)%(4*a)==0 or (p+s)%(4*a)==0 for s in [(x*x)%(4*a) for x in range(1,4*a,2)]) for a in primerange(3,40) for p in primerange(3,3000) if p%a!=0)
checkable.asserts: Euler's criterion form of reciprocity: a^m ≡ 1 mod p=2m+1 iff p ≡ ±(odd square) mod 4a

checkable.sympy: all(legendre_symbol(15,p)==(1 if p%60 in (1,17,49,53,59,43,11,7) else -1) for p in primerange(7,5000))
checkable.asserts: Next-page Example 4 (a=15) consistent with the same rule

transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially faithful to the image. The image heads the first example 'Exemplum I.' (Roman numeral) and the second 'Exemplum 2.' (Arabic); the transcription preserves this.
In Corollary 1 the image reads 'a^m − 1 = f^{2m} − 1', correctly transcribed.
